exam.subject: Physics
exam.title: Physics 2009

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I contains 30 questions. Each question carries 2 points. Use g = 10 m/s², c = 3×10⁸ m/s and the other constants printed on the paper.

source.scan: HP Scan image PDF; Part I MCQs typed from page images

exam.answer_key_note: No official key in the PDF. Answers solved independently with the printed constants. Part II not included in this batch. Q2 option order corrected to the scan: B is ML^{2}T^{-3}.

questions.stem: In some state of matter the molecules are widely separated and can move almost freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?

options.C: A liquid

explanation_steps: In a gas the intermolecular spacing is large and molecules move freely in all directions.
Solids have fixed positions; liquids are close together and not free in any direction. A fluid is liquid or gas, which is broader than the condition given. Answer: A.

questions.stem: If M, L, and T represent the dimensions of mass, length, and time, respectively, then which one of the following is the dimension of power?
explanation_steps: Power = work / time. Work has dimension ML^{2}T^{-2}.
Dividing by time gives ML^{2}T^{-3}.
On the paper that is option B. A is force, D is energy, E is ML^{2} (no time).

questions.stem: Which one of the following in SI unit of time is approximately equal to one day? (Give your answer in two significant figures)
explanation_steps: To two significant figures that is 8.6 × 10^{4} s, which is the value the stem asks for. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following physical quantities is a scalar?

options.C: Acceleration

explanation_steps: Displacement, velocity, acceleration and force all have direction (vectors).
Distance is magnitude only: a scalar. Answer: E.

questions.stem: In motion along a straight line, what does the slope in a velocity-time graph represent?

options.C: Acceleration

explanation_steps: Slope of a v–t graph is Δv/Δt, which is acceleration. Answer: C.

questions.stem: In a uniformly accelerated motion, which one of the following gives the correct relation between velocity and time?

options.A: Velocity is a quadratic function of time.
options.B: Velocity is inversely proportional to time.
options.C: Velocity is a cubic function of time.
options.D: Velocity is a linear function of time.

explanation_steps: v = u + at is linear in t when a is constant. Answer: D.

questions.stem: A freely falling object is dropped from a height of 20 m. What is the speed (in m/s) of the object when it just hits the ground?
explanation_steps: Dropped: u = 0. Use v^{2} = u^{2} + 2gh with g = 10 m/s^{2}.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: In a uniform circular motion of a particle its acceleration is directed toward the center of the circle.
options.B: In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its speed is constant.
options.C: In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its velocity is not constant.
options.D: In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its acceleration is constant.
options.E: In a uniform circular motion of a particle, its velocity is perpendicular to its acceleration.

explanation_steps: Centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude v^{2}/r but its direction always points to the centre, so the acceleration vector is not constant.
A, B, C and E are true of UCM. The incorrect statement is D.

questions.stem: A motorcar having a mass of 1,000 kg accelerates from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the net force (in newtons) acting on the car?
Normal force acts on the object ______ to the surface.

options.C: at 45°

explanation_steps: By definition the normal force is perpendicular (normal) to the contact surface. Answer: D.

questions.stem: An athlete of 80 kg mass climbs up to a height of 5 m with constant velocity. What is the work (in joules) done by the athlete in lifting his body?
explanation_steps: At constant velocity the net force is zero, but the work done by the athlete against gravity is mgh.

questions.stem: An object, initially at rest, explodes and splits up into two parts. How do the two parts move?

options.C: Perpendicular to each other.
options.D: One part remains at rest and the other is moving.
options.E: At an angle of 45° to each other.

explanation_steps: Initial momentum is zero. Conservation of momentum requires the two fragments to have equal and opposite momenta, so they move in opposite directions. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A force of 10 N acts on a 1 kg block placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The force acts on the block at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. Which one of the following gives the horizontal acceleration of the block in m/s²?
explanation_steps: Horizontal component F_x = 10 cos 60° = 10 × 1/2 = 5 N.
a_x = F_x / m = 5 / 1 = 5.0 m/s^{2}. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is incorrect for an image formed by a plane mirror?

options.C: The image is the same in size as the object.
options.D: The image and object distances from the mirror are equal.
options.E: The left hand of the object appears as right hand in the image.

explanation_steps: A plane mirror produces a virtual, laterally inverted image of the same size with |u| = |v|. It is not magnified. The incorrect statement is B.

questions.stem: If a ray of light is incident on a smooth surface at an angle of 40°, then what is the angle (in degrees) between the surface and the reflected ray?
explanation_steps: Angle of incidence is measured from the normal. Angle with the surface is 90° − 40° = 50°.
The reflected ray makes the same 50° angle with the surface. Answer: E.

questions.stem: If a ray of light goes from air to a medium of refractive index greater than one, then what will be the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence?

options.A: Larger than the angle of incidence.
options.B: Less than the angle of incidence.
options.C: Equal to the angle of incidence.
options.D: Not related to the angle of incidence.
options.E: Larger or equal to the angle of incidence.

explanation_steps: n_air ≈ 1 < n_medium, so the ray bends toward the normal: r < i. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A spherical concave mirror with an object at its center of curvature produces

options.A: A virtual image behind the mirror at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
options.B: A virtual image in front of the mirror at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
options.C: A real, upright, magnified image at an image distance equal to half of the radius of curvature (R).
options.D: A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to the radius of curvature (R).
options.E: A real, inverted, unmagnified image at an image distance equal to half of the radius of curvature (R).

explanation_steps: For a concave mirror, object at C (u = R = 2f) gives a real inverted image also at C, same size. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the dimension of the gravitational constant in the units of the SI system?
explanation_steps: From F = G m1 m2 / r^{2}, G = F r^{2} / (m1 m2).

questions.stem: A solid object is transferred from the Earth to the Moon. Which one of the following physical quantities of the object is changed?

options.C: The height

explanation_steps: Mass, volume and density of a solid are independent of g. Weight W = mg changes because g_Moon ≠ g_Earth. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Two charges, q1 and q2, interact with each other. If the sign of the charge q2 is changed to the opposite, but its magnitude remains the same, what can be said of the force acting on q1 due to q2?

options.A: The force changes its direction to the opposite only.
options.B: The magnitude of the force is increased twice with no change of its direction.
options.C: The magnitude of the force is decreased twice and its direction changes to the opposite.
options.E: The magnitude of the force is decreased twice with no change of its direction.

explanation_steps: Coulomb force magnitude k|q1 q2|/r^{2} is unchanged if only the sign of q2 flips.
The force reverses (attraction ↔ repulsion). Answer: A.

questions.stem: Charged particles are moving from terminal A to terminal B in a conductor. Suppose that the magnitude of velocity of each moving charge is doubled. Which one of the following is correct regarding the change of current between A and B?

options.A: The current changes its direction and its magnitude is doubled.
options.B: The magnitude of the current is doubled but no change in its direction.
options.C: The current changes its direction only.
options.D: The magnitude of the current is increased 4 times.
options.E: The magnitude of the current is doubled and its direction is changed to the opposite.

explanation_steps: I = nqAv_d. Doubling drift speed doubles I; the charges still travel A to B so the direction is unchanged. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not true about a current carrying conductor placed in the magnetic field?

options.A: The force on the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field.
options.B: The magnitude of the force acting on the current carrying conductor is directly proportional to the current on the conductor.
options.C: The force on the conductor is proportional to the length of the conductor.
options.D: The direction of the force changes to the opposite direction with the change of the current to the opposite direction.
options.E: There is no change in the direction of the force when magnetic field changes its direction.

explanation_steps: F = I L × B reverses if B reverses. Statement E is therefore not true. A-D follow from F = ILB sin theta and the right-hand rule.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is wrong about heat and temperature?

options.A: Temperature is a measure of degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
options.B: The SI unit of temperature is Kelvin.
options.C: Heat is energy in transit.
options.D: The SI unit of heat is calorie.
options.E: Heat flows naturally from a body at high temperature to a body at low temperature.

explanation_steps: The SI unit of heat (energy) is the joule, not the calorie. D is wrong.

questions.stem: An adiabatic process occurs

options.C: with no heat flow into or out of the system.

explanation_steps: Adiabatic means Q = 0: no heat enters or leaves the system. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid column is:

options.A: independent on the acceleration due to gravity.
options.C: independent on the shape of liquid's container.
options.D: independent on the atmospheric pressure on the top the column.
options.E: dependent on the area of the container.

explanation_steps: P = P0 + rho g h. This does not depend on the shape or area of the container. It does depend on g, density and P0. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The principle of the operation of a hydraulic jack is based on:

options.C: The law of energy conservation.

explanation_steps: A hydraulic jack transmits pressure undiminished through a confined liquid: Pascal's principle. Answer: E.

questions.stem: If the frequency of a broadcasting radio station is 3 MHz, then the wavelength (in meters) of the radio station is
explanation_steps: f = 3 MHz = 3 × 10^{6} Hz and c = 3 × 10^{8} m/s (given).

questions.stem: What physical phenomenon causes nodes to be formed during interference of waves?

options.C: Refraction

explanation_steps: Nodes are points of permanent destructive interference (zero amplitude). Answer: D.

questions.stem: Depending on the direction of vibration, waves can be classified into transverse and longitudinal. Which one of the following is incorrect about these waves?

options.A: A transverse wave is a wave in which the vibrations are at right angle to the direction of propagation of the wave.
options.B: A longitudinal wave is a wave in which the vibrations are along the direction of propagation of the wave.
options.C: Waves on the surface of water are longitudinal.

explanation_steps: Surface water waves are primarily transverse / mixed, not longitudinal. C is incorrect.

questions.stem: A sound wave with an intensity of 4 W/m² is passing through an area of 2 m². What is the intensity of the same wave (in W/m²) when it passes through an area of 1 cm²?
explanation_steps: Intensity is power per unit area of the wave; it does not change merely because a different patch of area is considered.
The intensity remains 4 W/m^{2}. Answer: D.
